@@ -1,314 +0,0 @@
-# ===========================================================================
-# SELF-HOSTING — the BEAM abstract-forms backend (whole module), in Rian
-# ===========================================================================
-# Goal (ADR-0063 §2, the default self-host target): build the Erlang abstract
-# forms for a whole module from the IR — the Rian-written counterpart of
-# `Rian.Beam`'s form generation. BEAM uses Erlang's NATIVE clause matching, so a
-# clause is just `{:clause, [pat forms], guard, body}` — no explicit test/bind
-# generation (unlike the JVM/JS ports); the patterns ARE the dispatch.
-#
-# Because Rian cannot spell operator atoms (`:+`/`:"=<"`) or Erlang variable atoms,
-# the port emits a `Form` sum carrying the Rian op / name / ctor as STRINGS; the
-# fixpoint (`test/rian/beam_module_fixpoint_test.exs`) inflates them to real forms
-# (the `erl_op`/`var_atom`/`to_snake` conventions), compiles the module via
-# `:compile.forms`, and RUNS it — asserting it behaves identically to
-# `Rian.Beam`. A numeric literal splits on its lexeme: a `.`/`e` marks a `Float64`
-# (parsed via `Prim.str_to_float` for correctly-rounded native parity), else `Int53`.
-# Lambdas lower to `FFun` (an Erlang `fun`, BEAM closing over captures) and variable
-# application to `FApply`; the driver's `resolve_apply` tells a fun-valued var from a
-# local call. The remaining out-of-scope prims are the i64 overflow ops + `float_repr`.
-# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-
-mod Beam do
-  # ── Core (supported subset) ──
-  type Core := CNum(String)
-             | CStr(String)
-             | CChar(Int53)
-             | CId(String)
-             | CAtom(String)
-             | CUnary(String, Core)
-             | CBin(String, Core, Core)
-             | CCall(String, Vec(Core))
-             | CLambda(Vec(String), Core)
-             | CApply(Core, Vec(Core))
-             | CRemote(String, String, Vec(Core))
-             | CDot(Core, String)
-             | CStruct(String, Vec(SFld))
-             | CMap(Vec(SFld))
-             | CTuple(Vec(Core))
-             | CList(Vec(Core), Tail)
-             | CIf(Core, Block, Block)
-             | CCase(Core, Vec(Arm))
-
-  type Tail := TClose | TTail(Core)
-  type SFld := SFld(String, Core)
-  type Block := Block(Vec(Stmt))
-  type Stmt := SBind(String, Core) | STypedBind(String, String, Core) | SExpr(Core)
-  type Arm := Arm(Pat, Guard, Block)
-
-  type Pat := PWild
-            | PVar(String)
-            | PInt(Int53)
-            | PStr(String)
-            | PChar(Int53)
-            | PAtom(String)
-            | PCtor(String, Vec(Pat))
-            | PTuple(Vec(Pat))
-            | PStructP(String, Vec(FldP))
-            | PList(Vec(Pat), PTail)
-
-  type PTail := PtlClose | PtlTail(Pat)
-  type FldP := FP(String, Pat)
-  type Guard := GNone | GSome(Core)
-  type Clause := Clause(Vec(Pat), Guard, Block)
-  type Func := Func(String, Int53, Vec(Clause))
-
-  # ── Form (output; strings inflated by the fixpoint) ──
-  type Form := FInt(Int53)
-             | FFloat(Float64)
-             | FStr(String)
-             | FVar(String)
-             | FAtom(String)
-             | FCtorN(String)
-             | FCtor(String, Vec(Form))
-             | FOp1(String, Form)
-             | FOp2(String, Form, Form)
-             | FConcat(Form, Form)
-             | FBinAll(Vec(Form))
-             | FCharBin(Form)
-             | FCall(String, Vec(Form))
-             | FFun(Vec(String), Form)
-             | FApply(Form, Vec(Form))
-             | FRemote(String, String, Vec(Form))
-             | FTuple(Vec(Form))
-             | FStruct(String, Vec(FFld))
-             | FMap(Vec(FFld))
-             | FMapPat(String, Vec(FFldP))
-             | FNil
-             | FCons(Form, Form)
-             | FIf(Form, Vec(Form), Vec(Form))
-             | FCase(Form, Vec(FClause))
-             | FMatch(String, Form)
-
-  type FFld := FFld(String, Form)
-  type FFldP := FFP(String, Form)
-  type GForm := GfNone | GfSome(Form)
-  type FClause := FClause(Vec(Form), GForm, Vec(Form))
-  type FFunc := FFunc(String, Int53, Vec(FClause))
-
-  pub def compile_forms(Vec(Func)) Vec(FFunc)
-  pub def compile_forms([]) := []
-  pub def compile_forms([f | rest]) := [func_form(f) | compile_forms(rest)]
-
-  def func_form(Func) FFunc
-  def func_form(Func(name, arity, clauses)) := FFunc(name, arity, clause_forms(clauses))
-
-  def clause_forms(Vec(Clause)) Vec(FClause)
-  def clause_forms([]) := []
-  def clause_forms([c | rest]) := [clause_form(c) | clause_forms(rest)]
-
-  def clause_form(Clause) FClause
-  def clause_form(Clause(pats, guard, body)) :=
-    FClause(pat_forms(pats), gform(guard), block_forms(body))
-
-  # ── patterns -> forms (native Erlang dispatch) ──
-  def pat_forms(Vec(Pat)) Vec(Form)
-  def pat_forms([]) := []
-  def pat_forms([p | rest]) := [pat_form(p) | pat_forms(rest)]
-
-  def pat_form(Pat) Form
-  def pat_form(PWild) := FVar("_")
-  def pat_form(PVar(n)) := FVar(n)
-  def pat_form(PInt(v)) := FInt(v)
-  def pat_form(PStr(s)) := FStr(s)
-  def pat_form(PChar(cp)) := FInt(cp)
-  def pat_form(PAtom(a)) := FAtom(a)
-  def pat_form(PCtor(c, [])) := FCtorN(c)
-  def pat_form(PCtor(c, args)) := FCtor(c, pat_forms(args))
-  def pat_form(PStructP(name, flds)) := FMapPat(name, fld_pat_forms(flds))
-  def pat_form(PTuple(es)) := FTuple(pat_forms(es))
-  def pat_form(PList(es, PtlClose)) := list_form(pat_forms(es), FNil)
-  def pat_form(PList(es, PtlTail(t))) := list_form(pat_forms(es), pat_form(t))
-
-  def list_form(Vec(Form), Form) Form
-  def list_form([], tail) := tail
-  def list_form([x | rest], tail) := FCons(x, list_form(rest, tail))
-
-  def gform(Guard) GForm
-  def gform(GNone) := GfNone
-  def gform(GSome(g)) := GfSome(expr_form(g))
-
-  # ── body / statements ──
-  def block_forms(Block) Vec(Form)
-  def block_forms(Block(stmts)) := stmt_forms(stmts)
-
-  def stmt_forms(Vec(Stmt)) Vec(Form)
-  def stmt_forms([]) := []
-  def stmt_forms([s | rest]) := [stmt_form(s) | stmt_forms(rest)]
-
-  def stmt_form(Stmt) Form
-  def stmt_form(SBind(n, e)) := FMatch(n, expr_form(e))
-  def stmt_form(STypedBind(n, _, e)) := FMatch(n, expr_form(e))
-  def stmt_form(SExpr(e)) := expr_form(e)
-
-  # ── expressions -> forms ──
-  def expr_form(Core) Form
-  # a numeric literal carries its lexeme as text (like Rian.Beam's `%ENum{text}`);
-  # a `.` or `e`/`E` marks a Float64 — parsed with correctly-rounded native parse
-  # (`Prim.str_to_float`), an `Int53` otherwise. `_` separators are dropped either way.
-  def expr_form(CNum(t))
-    if float_lex(t) do
-      FFloat(Prim.str_to_float(drop_us(t)))
-    else
-      FInt(parse_int(t))
-    end
-  end
-  def expr_form(CStr(s)) := FStr(s)
-  def expr_form(CChar(cp)) := FInt(cp)
-  def expr_form(CId("true")) := FAtom("true")
-  def expr_form(CId("false")) := FAtom("false")
-  def expr_form(CId(x))
-    if pascal(x) do
-      FCtorN(x)
-    else
-      FVar(x)
-    end
-  end
-  def expr_form(CAtom(a)) := FAtom(a)
-  def expr_form(CUnary(op, x)) := FOp1(op, expr_form(x))
-  # `<>` is NOT an Erlang operator — it is binary construction `<<L/binary, R/binary>>`
-  # (Rian.Beam). MUST precede the generic CBin clause (which would emit a bad FOp2).
-  def expr_form(CBin("<>", l, r)) := FConcat(expr_form(l), expr_form(r))
-  def expr_form(CBin(op, l, r)) := FOp2(op, expr_form(l), expr_form(r))
-  # portable-prelude prims (ADR-0047) — each lowers to the SAME native Erlang form
-  # Rian.Beam uses, so the composed build is byte-equivalent: str_chars →
-  # String.to_charlist, str_from_chars → List.to_string, char_code → identity
-  # (a Char IS its codepoint on the BEAM). MUST precede the generic CCall clause.
-  def expr_form(CCall("__prim_str_concat", [a, b])) := FConcat(expr_form(a), expr_form(b))
-  def expr_form(CCall("__prim_str_to_atom", [s])) := FRemote("Elixir.String", "to_atom", [expr_form(s)])
-  def expr_form(CCall("__prim_str_to_float", [s])) := FRemote("erlang", "binary_to_float", [expr_form(s)])
-  def expr_form(CCall("__prim_int_to_string", [n])) := FRemote("erlang", "integer_to_binary", [expr_form(n)])
-  def expr_form(CCall("__prim_str_chars", [s])) := FRemote("Elixir.String", "to_charlist", [expr_form(s)])
-  def expr_form(CCall("__prim_str_from_chars", [cs])) := FRemote("Elixir.List", "to_string", [expr_form(cs)])
-  def expr_form(CCall("__prim_char_code", [c])) := expr_form(c)
-  def expr_form(CCall("__prim_int_to_float", [n])) := FRemote("erlang", "float", [expr_form(n)])
-  # a Char's single-character UTF-8 string is `<<cp/utf8>>` (a Char IS its codepoint).
-  def expr_form(CCall("__prim_char_to_string", [c])) := FCharBin(expr_form(c))
-  # variadic single-shot join (ADR-0069 §6): ONE binary from all parts.
-  def expr_form(CCall("__prim_str_concat_all", args)) := FBinAll(expr_forms(args))
-  # portable Map ops -> a BEAM map literal + `:maps` calls (arg order: key, [val,] map).
-  def expr_form(CCall("__prim_map_new", [])) := FMap([])
-  def expr_form(CCall("__prim_map_get", [m, k])) := FRemote("maps", "get", [expr_form(k), expr_form(m)])
-  def expr_form(CCall("__prim_map_put", [m, k, v])) := FRemote("maps", "put", [expr_form(k), expr_form(v), expr_form(m)])
-  def expr_form(CCall("__prim_map_has", [m, k])) := FRemote("maps", "is_key", [expr_form(k), expr_form(m)])
-  # Float64 shortest round-trip repr (ADR-0069 Show.float): native float_to_binary/2.
-  def expr_form(CCall("__prim_float_repr", [n])) := FRemote("erlang", "float_to_binary", [expr_form(n), FCons(FAtom("short"), FNil)])
-  # i64 two's-complement overflow ops (ADR-0035/0064): bind the sum once in a fun, then
-  # project — wrap to [-2^63, 2^63), saturate to the i64 bounds, or `Some`/`None` on overflow.
-  def expr_form(CCall("__prim_wrapping_add", [a, b])) := i64_ovf("wrapping", expr_form(a), expr_form(b))
-  def expr_form(CCall("__prim_saturating_add", [a, b])) := i64_ovf("saturating", expr_form(a), expr_form(b))
-  def expr_form(CCall("__prim_checked_add", [a, b])) := i64_ovf("checked", expr_form(a), expr_form(b))
-  def expr_form(CCall(f, args))
-    if pascal(f) do
-      FCtor(f, expr_forms(args))
-    else
-      FCall(f, expr_forms(args))
-    end
-  end
-  # a cross-module (remote) call `Mod.fun(args)` — what the composition driver uses
-  # to reach the verified lexer/decl/beam modules. Lowers to the same `{:call, …,
-  # {:remote, …}, …}` form Rian.Beam emits for qualified calls.
-  def expr_form(CRemote(m, f, args)) := FRemote(m, f, expr_forms(args))
-  # struct field access `value.field` — a struct is a tagged map keyed by field-name
-  # atoms (Rian.Beam), so reading a field is `maps:get(:field, value)`.
-  def expr_form(CDot(h, f)) := FRemote("maps", "get", [FAtom(f), expr_form(h)])
-  def expr_form(CLambda(ps, b)) := FFun(ps, expr_form(b))
-  def expr_form(CApply(c, args)) := FApply(expr_form(c), expr_forms(args))
-  def expr_form(CTuple(es)) := FTuple(expr_forms(es))
-  # named struct construction `Name(f: v, …)` — a tagged map (the driver's inflater
-  # adds the `__struct__` field + snake tag, matching Rian.Beam.expr_form).
-  def expr_form(CStruct(name, fields)) := FStruct(name, fld_forms(fields))
-  # map literal -> a plain Erlang map form (no `__struct__` tag); reuses fld_forms.
-  def expr_form(CMap(fields)) := FMap(fld_forms(fields))
-  def expr_form(CList(es, TClose)) := list_form(expr_forms(es), FNil)
-  def expr_form(CList(es, TTail(t))) := list_form(expr_forms(es), expr_form(t))
-  def expr_form(CIf(c, t, e)) := FIf(expr_form(c), block_forms(t), block_forms(e))
-  def expr_form(CCase(scrut, arms)) := FCase(expr_form(scrut), arm_forms(arms))
-
-  def arm_forms(Vec(Arm)) Vec(FClause)
-  def arm_forms([]) := []
-  def arm_forms([a | rest]) := [arm_form(a) | arm_forms(rest)]
-
-  def arm_form(Arm) FClause
-  def arm_form(Arm(pat, guard, body)) := FClause([pat_form(pat)], gform(guard), block_forms(body))
-
-  def expr_forms(Vec(Core)) Vec(Form)
-  def expr_forms([]) := []
-  def expr_forms([x | rest]) := [expr_form(x) | expr_forms(rest)]
-
-  def fld_forms(Vec(SFld)) Vec(FFld)
-  def fld_forms([]) := []
-  def fld_forms([SFld(k, v) | rest]) := [FFld(k, expr_form(v)) | fld_forms(rest)]
-
-  def fld_pat_forms(Vec(FldP)) Vec(FFldP)
-  def fld_pat_forms([]) := []
-  def fld_pat_forms([FP(f, p) | rest]) := [FFP(f, pat_form(p)) | fld_pat_forms(rest)]
-
-  # ── i64 overflow projection (mirrors Rian.Beam.i64_overflow/i64_project) ──
-  # bind the sum once in a 1-clause fun, then project per kind. Masks exceed Int53 but
-  # are exact BEAM bignums at runtime; FInt only carries them through to the form.
-  def i64_ovf(kind String, a Form, b Form) Form := FApply(FFun(["OvfSum"], i64_project(kind, FVar("OvfSum"))), [FOp2("+", a, b)])
-
-  def i64_project(String, Form) Form
-  def i64_project("wrapping", sv) := FCase(FOp2(">=", i64_low(sv), FInt(9223372036854775808)), [FClause([FAtom("true")], GfNone, [FOp2("-", i64_low(sv), FInt(18446744073709551616))]), FClause([FAtom("false")], GfNone, [i64_low(sv)])])
-  def i64_project("saturating", sv) := FRemote("erlang", "max", [FRemote("erlang", "min", [sv, FInt(9223372036854775807)]), i64_min()])
-  def i64_project("checked", sv) := FCase(FOp2("and", FOp2(">=", sv, i64_min()), FOp2("<=", sv, FInt(9223372036854775807))), [FClause([FAtom("true")], GfNone, [FCtor("Some", [sv])]), FClause([FAtom("false")], GfNone, [FCtorN("None")])])
-
-  # the low 64 bits (`sum band (2^64-1)`); i64_min as `-(2^63)` (FInt is non-negative).
-  def i64_low(sv Form) Form := FOp2("band", sv, FInt(18446744073709551615))
-  def i64_min() Form := FOp1("-", FInt(9223372036854775808))
-
-  # ── helpers (portable, FFI-free) ──
-  def parse_int(s String) Int53 := digits(Prim.str_chars(s), 0)
-
-  # a numeric lexeme is a float iff it carries a `.` or an exponent marker.
-  def float_lex(s String) Bool := has_float_marker(Prim.str_chars(s))
-  def has_float_marker(Vec(Int53)) Bool
-  def has_float_marker([]) := false
-  def has_float_marker([c | rest])
-    if c == 46 or c == 101 or c == 69 do
-      true
-    else
-      has_float_marker(rest)
-    end
-  end
-
-  # drop `_` digit separators (code 95) — `binary_to_float` rejects them.
-  def drop_us(s String) String := Prim.str_from_chars(no_us(Prim.str_chars(s)))
-  def no_us(Vec(Int53)) Vec(Int53)
-  def no_us([]) := []
-  def no_us([c | rest])
-    if c == 95 do
-      no_us(rest)
-    else
-      [c | no_us(rest)]
-    end
-  end
-
-  def digits(Vec(Int53), Int53) Int53
-  def digits([], acc) := acc
-  def digits([c | rest], acc)
-    if c == 95 do
-      digits(rest, acc)
-    else
-      digits(rest, acc * 10 + c - 48)
-    end
-  end
-
-  def pascal(s String) Bool
-    case Prim.str_chars(s) do
-      [c | _] -> c >= 65 and c <= 90
-      [] -> false
-    end
-  end
-end

@@ -1,121 +0,0 @@
-# ===========================================================================
-# SELF-HOSTING SPIKE — the capability→Rust lowering (FULL), written in Rian
-# ===========================================================================
-# Goal (ADR-0063 §2, the capability checker; ADR-0055/0025): the complete
-# capability→Rust parameter-type mapping + BEAM legality — the Rian-written
-# counterpart of `Rian.Capability.rust_param/2` and `beam_legal!/1`,
-# fixpoint-locked against them in `test/rian/cap_fixpoint_test.exs` over the FULL
-# type vocabulary: every `Copy` width, `String`, nominal types, nested `Vec(...)`,
-# and parametric generics `Name(A, B, …)` — including the reference's quirk that
-# `val` of a generic borrows the *unlowered* source spelling.
-#
-# The capability stage's responsibility is the cap+type→Rust MAPPING; it consumes
-# a type in the IR's structured form (`Ty`). String tokenisation of a type
-# annotation (`"Vec(Int32)"` → `TVec(TScalar("Int32"))`) belongs to the type
-# parser, not here — the reference re-parses the string only because the IR stores
-# types as strings. The mapping itself is reproduced in full.
-#
-# The BEAM linearity check (use-at-most-once for iso/ref) is native typestate, not
-# part of this signature mapping — it stays out of scope (ADR-0055).
-# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-
-mod Cap do
-  # A reference capability (ADR-0055).
-  type Cap := Iso | Val | Ref | Tag
-
-  # A type in structured (already-tokenised) form. `TScalar` carries the source
-  # width name; `TGen` carries its raw source spelling too (the reference borrows
-  # a generic unlowered — see `borrowed`).
-  type Ty := TScalar(String)
-           | TString
-           | TNom(String)
-           | TVec(Ty)
-           | TGen(String, Vec(Ty), String)
-
-  # The `Copy` set is exactly the structured scalars; everything else borrows.
-  def copyt(Ty) Bool
-  def copyt(TScalar(_)) := true
-  def copyt(TString) := false
-  def copyt(TNom(_)) := false
-  def copyt(TVec(_)) := false
-  def copyt(TGen(_, _, _)) := false
-
-  # Source width name -> Rust scalar spelling (the reference `rust_scalar`). `Int53`
-  # is the JS-safe integer; on Rust it is `i64`.
-  def scalar(String) String
-  def scalar("Int53") := "i64"
-  def scalar("Int8") := "i8"
-  def scalar("Int16") := "i16"
-  def scalar("Int32") := "i32"
-  def scalar("Int64") := "i64"
-  def scalar("Int128") := "i128"
-  def scalar("UInt8") := "u8"
-  def scalar("UInt16") := "u16"
-  def scalar("UInt32") := "u32"
-  def scalar("UInt64") := "u64"
-  def scalar("UInt128") := "u128"
-  def scalar("Float32") := "f32"
-  def scalar("Float64") := "f64"
-  def scalar("Bool") := "bool"
-  def scalar("Char") := "char"
-
-  # The owned Rust spelling (`iso`/`ref`/`tag` base, `val` of a `Copy` type).
-  def owned(Ty) String
-  def owned(TScalar(s)) := scalar(s)
-  def owned(TString) := "String"
-  def owned(TNom(s)) := s
-  def owned(TVec(t)) := "Vec<" <> owned(t) <> ">"
-  def owned(TGen(name, args, _)) := gen_head(name) <> "<" <> owned_args(args) <> ">"
-
-  # `Map(K, V)` (the `Dict` prelude's backing, ADR-0047) -> `std::collections::HashMap`;
-  # every other generic keeps its source name.
-  def gen_head(String) String
-  def gen_head("Map") := "std::collections::HashMap"
-  def gen_head(name) := name
-
-  # Lower a generic's type arguments, comma-separated.
-  def owned_args(Vec(Ty)) String
-  def owned_args([]) := ""
-  def owned_args([t]) := owned(t)
-  def owned_args([t | rest]) := owned(t) <> ", " <> owned_args(rest)
-
-  # The borrowed Rust spelling (`val` of a non-`Copy` type). Note the reference
-  # quirk: a generic is borrowed *unlowered* (`&Option(Int64)`, from `rust_name`'s
-  # passthrough), so `TGen` borrows its raw source spelling.
-  def borrowed(Ty) String
-  def borrowed(TString) := "&str"
-  def borrowed(TVec(t)) := "&[" <> owned(t) <> "]"
-  def borrowed(TScalar(s)) := "&" <> scalar(s)
-  def borrowed(TNom(s)) := "&" <> s
-  # a generic borrows its raw source spelling (`rustify` rewrites a user type later), EXCEPT
-  # `Map`, which has no user definition to rewrite — it lowers to `&HashMap<…>` directly.
-  def borrowed(TGen(name, args, raw)) := borrow_gen(name, owned_args(args), raw)
-
-  def borrow_gen(String, String, String) String
-  def borrow_gen("Map", inner, _) := "&std::collections::HashMap<" <> inner <> ">"
-  def borrow_gen(_, _, raw) := "&" <> raw
-
-  # `val` lowers by value when the type is `Copy`, else by shared borrow.
-  def val_param(t Ty) String
-    if copyt(t) do
-      owned(t)
-    else
-      borrowed(t)
-    end
-  end
-
-  # capability + type -> Rust parameter spelling.
-  pub def rust_param(Cap, Ty) String
-  pub def rust_param(Iso, t) := owned(t)
-  pub def rust_param(Val, t) := val_param(t)
-  pub def rust_param(Ref, t) := "&mut " <> owned(t)
-  pub def rust_param(Tag, t) := "&" <> owned(t)
-
-  # BEAM legality: the portable core is val/iso/tag; `ref` (`&mut`) is rejected
-  # (P5). The reference raises on `ref`; reported as a Bool here.
-  pub def beam_legal(Cap) Bool
-  pub def beam_legal(Ref) := false
-  pub def beam_legal(Iso) := true
-  pub def beam_legal(Val) := true
-  pub def beam_legal(Tag) := true
-end

@@ -1,1427 +0,0 @@
-# ===========================================================================
-# SELF-HOSTING SPIKE — the real type checker (inference), written in Rian
-# ===========================================================================
-# Goal (ADR-0063 §2, the type-checker stage): infer the type of an expression —
-# a slice of the REAL `Rian.Check.infer/3` (not the toy-language `selfhost_check`
-# checker). Fixpoint-locked against `Rian.Check.infer` in
-# `test/rian/checker_infer_fixpoint_test.exs`.
-#
-# Inference rules (ADR-0064): a numeric literal is `Int53`, or `Float64` if it
-# carries a `.`/`e`/`E`; a string is `String`, a char `Char`, `true`/`false` `Bool`;
-# unary `-` passes the operand type through and `not` is `Bool`; a binary op's result
-# is determined by the op — comparisons/`and`/`or` are `Bool`, `<>` is `String`, `/`
-# is `Float64`, and `+ - * div rem` over integers are `Int53`. The determinate
-# primitive intrinsics infer their result type (`__prim_char_code` → `Int53`,
-# `__prim_int_to_float` → `Float64`, `__prim_str_to_atom` → `Symbol`,
-# `__prim_char_to_string`/`__prim_str_concat_all` → `String`). An unbound identifier
-# or a general (non-prim) call is `unknown` — the checker is deliberately
-# conservative and does NOT guess.
-#
-# A typing ENVIRONMENT (name -> type) is threaded through inference: a bound
-# variable resolves to its declared type (`infer_env/2`; `infer/1` is the empty-env
-# convenience). Arithmetic is OPERAND-DIRECTED (Rian.Check's `arith_type`): an int
-# literal adopts a concrete-integer neighbour's width, `Char` ordinals widen to
-# `Int53`, float arithmetic is `Float64`, and a mismatch (`Int53 + Float64`) is
-# `unknown`. `if` infers the LUB-join of its branches (each a single-expression
-# block): the branches climb to their LUB via the full numeric-widening `join`
-# (`Int8`⊔`Int53`=`Int53`, `Int53`⊔`Float64`=`Float64`, `UInt8`⊔`Int64`=`Int64`), an
-# integer literal adopts a non-literal integer branch, and an incompatible pair is
-# `unknown`. `case` infers the LUB-join of its arm bodies, each under the env
-# flow-NARROWED by the arm pattern (a variable binds the scrutinee's type). A list
-# literal infers `Vec(T)` when its elements (and any cons tail) LUB-join to a concrete
-# `T`. A lambda infers its arrow type `Fn(arg.., body)` (an unannotated param is `_`),
-# the body inferred under the param bindings. A general call resolves a function-typed
-# env var (higher-order: `g(5)` with `g : Fn(Int64,Int64)` -> `Int64`), an applied
-# constructor (`ic.ctors`), or a non-generic named function's return (`ic.funs`); a
-# bare identifier resolves a nullary constructor's sum type (`ic.ctors`) when not a
-# bound variable. Covered Core nodes (12, FULL): CNum/CStr/CChar/CId/CUnary/CBin/CCall/
-# CIf/CBlock/CCase/CList/CLambda. Both a typing env AND an inference context `ic`
-# (`:ctors`/`:funs`/`:fsigs`/`:tdefs`) are threaded through (`infer_ic/3`; `infer_env/2`
-# and `infer/1` are empty-context conveniences). The join LUB is complete (numeric
-# widening + the parametric covariant join). GENERIC function-return instantiation
-# (`ic.fsigs` with type variables, ADR-0042 — unify declared params with inferred arg
-# types, substitute the bound tvars in the return, else `unknown`) and constructor-
-# pattern field narrowing (`ic.tdefs` — a `case` arm's ctor pattern binds each field
-# variable to its declared field type) are now both implemented, matching
-# Rian.Check.infer/3 over the whole inference-context axis. See ADR-0063.
-# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-
-mod Checker do
-  type Core := CNum(String)
-             | CStr(String)
-             | CChar(Int53)
-             | CId(String)
-             | CUnary(String, Core)
-             | CBin(String, Core, Core)
-             | CCall(String, Vec(Core))
-             | CIf(Core, Core, Core)
-             | CBlock(Vec(Stmt))
-             | CCase(Core, Vec(Arm))
-             | CList(Vec(Core), Tail)
-             | CLambda(Vec(Param), Core)
-             | CAtom(String)
-             | CTuple(Vec(Core))
-
-  # a list literal's tail: closed (`[a, b]`) or a cons tail expression (`[h | t]`).
-  type Tail := TClose | TCons(Core)
-  # a lambda parameter: a name + an optional type annotation (absent -> `_`).
-  type Param := LP(String, PType)
-  type PType := PtNone | PtSome(String)
-
-  # a block statement: a `name := e` bind (extends the env) or a bare expression;
-  # the block's type is its last expression's (Rian.Check.infer_block).
-  type Stmt := SBind(String, Core) | SExpr(Core) | STypedBind(String, String, Core)
-  # a `case` arm: a pattern + a single-expression body (the guard is type-irrelevant).
-  # The pattern flow-NARROWS the env: a variable binds the scrutinee's type.
-  type Arm := CArm(Pat, Core)
-  type Pat := PVar(String) | PCtor(String, Vec(Pat)) | POther
-  # a generic function signature (ADR-0042): declared parameter types, return type,
-  # and the `forall` type variables — the basis for instantiating a generic return.
-  type FSig := FSig(Vec(String), String, Vec(String))
-  type FsOpt := FsSome(FSig) | FsNone
-  # one `tvar -> concrete type` binding accumulated while unifying params with args.
-  type Bind := Bnd(String, String)
-  # error set #4 (protocol bounds, ADR-0042 §2): a bounded generic's signature — its
-  # `tvars`, declared param types, and `tvar: P + Q` bounds — keyed by function name in
-  # `fbounds`; `ProtoBound` is one `tvar -> protocols` pair; `TyLk` is a bind-lookup result.
-  type FBnd := FB(Vec(String), Vec(String), Vec(ProtoBound))
-  type ProtoBound := PBound(String, Vec(String))
-  type TyLk := TyHit(String) | TyMiss
-  # error set #5 (`Result(T, E)` error-set check, ADR-0040 §4): the declared error-tag set of a
-  # `Result(T, E)` return, or none when the return is not a `Result(T, E)`.
-  type EsOpt := EsNone | EsSome(Vec(String))
-  # collecting a maximal word-run while tokenizing a type string.
-  type WordTake := WT(String, Vec(Int53))
-  # a branch/arm with its inferred type, for the LUB join (branch_join).
-  type BPair := BP(Core, String)
-  # a numeric type decomposed into kind ("int"/"uint"/"float") + bit width, or none.
-  type NumKind := NkNone | Nk(String, Int53)
-  # a parametric type `Name(arg, …)` decomposed into its name + argument types, or none.
-  type PpRes := PpNone | Pp(String, Vec(String))
-  # error-set #2 (return type) helpers: an optional constant-integer value, an optional
-  # `Vec(_)` element type, and a fixed-width integer's two's-complement bounds.
-  type IntOpt := INone | ISome(Int53)
-  type VecOpt := VNone | VSome(String)
-  type BoundOpt := BNone | B(Int53, Int53)
-
-  # A binary op's result type, keyed by the operator (the integer slice):
-  # comparisons/`and`/`or`/`in` -> Bool, `<>` -> String, `/` -> Float64, the
-  # arithmetic ops over integers -> Int53.
-  def bin_ty(String) String
-  def bin_ty("==") := "Bool"
-  def bin_ty("!=") := "Bool"
-  def bin_ty("<") := "Bool"
-  def bin_ty("<=") := "Bool"
-  def bin_ty(">") := "Bool"
-  def bin_ty(">=") := "Bool"
-  def bin_ty("and") := "Bool"
-  def bin_ty("or") := "Bool"
-  def bin_ty("in") := "Bool"
-  def bin_ty("<>") := "String"
-  def bin_ty("/") := "Float64"
-  def bin_ty("+") := "Int53"
-  def bin_ty("-") := "Int53"
-  def bin_ty("*") := "Int53"
-  def bin_ty("div") := "Int53"
-  def bin_ty("rem") := "Int53"
-
-  # A numeric literal: `Float64` if it carries a decimal point or an exponent marker
-  # (`.`/`e`/`E`), else the portable `Int53` (ADR-0064 — mirrors Rian.Check's ENum).
-  def num_ty(t String) String
-  def num_ty(t)
-    if float_mark(Prim.str_chars(t)) do
-      "Float64"
-    else
-      "Int53"
-    end
-  end
-
-  def float_mark(Vec(Int53)) Bool
-  def float_mark([]) := false
-  def float_mark([c | rest])
-    if c == 46 or c == 101 or c == 69 do
-      true
-    else
-      float_mark(rest)
-    end
-  end
-
-  # ── operand-directed arithmetic result (ADR-0034/0036; mirrors Rian.Check.arith_type) ──
-  # `+ - * div rem`. An integer-literal operand is width-flexible — it ADOPTS a
-  # concrete-integer neighbour's width (`Int8 + 1` is `Int8`, not the literal's
-  # default); two non-literal operands UNIFY their ordinal bases (`Char` → `Int53`,
-  # so `'9' - '0'` is `Int53`); a mismatch (e.g. `Int53 + Float64`, no implicit
-  # int→float) is conservatively `unknown`.
-  def arith_op(op String) Bool := op == "+" or op == "-" or op == "*" or op == "div" or op == "rem"
-
-  def arith_type(l Core, r Core, lt String, rt String) String
-  def arith_type(l, r, lt, rt)
-    if int_lit_expr(l) and int_type(rt) do
-      ordinal_base(rt)
-    else
-      arith_type2(r, lt, rt)
-    end
-  end
-
-  def arith_type2(r Core, lt String, rt String) String
-  def arith_type2(r, lt, rt)
-    if int_lit_expr(r) and int_type(lt) do
-      ordinal_base(lt)
-    else
-      conservative(unify(ordinal_base(lt), ordinal_base(rt)))
-    end
-  end
-
-  # a constant integer expression of literals (a bare int literal, negation, or
-  # arithmetic of such) — the operand that may adopt a typed neighbour's width.
-  def int_lit_expr(Core) Bool
-  def int_lit_expr(CNum(t)) := int_literal(t)
-  def int_lit_expr(CUnary("-", a)) := int_lit_expr(a)
-  def int_lit_expr(CBin(op, l, r)) := arith_op(op) and int_lit_expr(l) and int_lit_expr(r)
-  # an `if`/`case` branch is a single-expression block (`do 0 end`)
-  def int_lit_expr(CBlock([SExpr(e)])) := int_lit_expr(e)
-  def int_lit_expr(_) := false
-
-  def int_literal(t String) Bool := not float_mark(Prim.str_chars(t))
-
-  # a concrete integer type: `^U?Int\d*$` (`Int`, `Int8`…`Int128`, `UInt8`…).
-  def int_type(t String) Bool := int_word(skip_u(Prim.str_chars(t)))
-
-  def skip_u(Vec(Int53)) Vec(Int53)
-  def skip_u(['U' | rest]) := rest
-  def skip_u(cs) := cs
-
-  def int_word(Vec(Int53)) Bool
-  def int_word(['I', 'n', 't' | rest]) := all_digits(rest)
-  def int_word(_) := false
-
-  def all_digits(Vec(Int53)) Bool
-  def all_digits([]) := true
-  def all_digits([c | rest]) := c >= 48 and c <= 57 and all_digits(rest)
-
-  # `Char`'s ordinal base is its codepoint width `Int53` (ADR-0036); else passthrough.
-  def ordinal_base(t String) String
-  def ordinal_base("Char") := "Int53"
-  def ordinal_base(t) := t
-
-  # the unification kernel (ADR-0033): equal types unify; `unknown` is the identity;
-  # else a mismatch (`"mismatch"` sentinel). Fn-structural unify is out of scope here.
-  def unify(a String, b String) String
-  def unify(a, b)
-    if a == b do
-      a
-    else
-      unify_unknown(a, b)
-    end
-  end
-
-  def unify_unknown(a String, b String) String
-  def unify_unknown(a, b)
-    if a == "unknown" do
-      b
-    else
-      pick_b_or_mismatch(a, b)
-    end
-  end
-
-  def pick_b_or_mismatch(a String, b String) String
-  def pick_b_or_mismatch(a, b)
-    if b == "unknown" do
-      a
-    else
-      "mismatch"
-    end
-  end
-
-  def conservative(t String) String := if t == "mismatch" do "unknown" else t end
-
-  # Infer the type of a Core node in the empty env + empty inference context.
-  pub def infer(Core) String
-  pub def infer(c) := infer_ic(c, Prim.map_new(), Prim.map_new())
-
-  # Infer under a typing env only (empty inference context).
-  pub def infer_env(Core, Dict(String, String)) String
-  pub def infer_env(c, env) := infer_ic(c, env, Prim.map_new())
-
-  # Infer under a typing env AND an inference context `ic` (a map with `:ctors`
-  # name->type and `:funs` name->return-type). A bound id resolves to its env type,
-  # else a nullary constructor's sum type (`ic.ctors`), else `unknown`. A call
-  # resolves a function-typed env var (higher-order), else an applied constructor
-  # (`ic.ctors`), else a non-generic named function's return (`ic.funs`). (Generic-
-  # return instantiation and constructor-pattern field narrowing — needing `ic.fsigs`
-  # / `ic.tdefs` — are the remaining tail.)
-  pub def infer_ic(Core, Dict(String, String), Dict(Symbol, Dict(String, String))) String
-  pub def infer_ic(CNum(t), _, _) := num_ty(t)
-  pub def infer_ic(CStr(_), _, _) := "String"
-  pub def infer_ic(CChar(_), _, _) := "Char"
-  pub def infer_ic(CId("true"), _, _) := "Bool"
-  pub def infer_ic(CId("false"), _, _) := "Bool"
-  pub def infer_ic(CId(x), env, ic) := id_ty(x, env, ic)
-  pub def infer_ic(CUnary("not", _), _, _) := "Bool"
-  pub def infer_ic(CUnary("-", x), env, ic) := infer_ic(x, env, ic)
-  pub def infer_ic(CBin(op, l, r), env, ic)
-    if arith_op(op) do
-      arith_type(l, r, infer_ic(l, env, ic), infer_ic(r, env, ic))
-    else
-      bin_ty(op)
-    end
-  end
-  pub def infer_ic(CCall("__prim_char_code", [_]), _, _) := "Int53"
-  pub def infer_ic(CCall("__prim_int_to_float", [_]), _, _) := "Float64"
-  pub def infer_ic(CCall("__prim_str_to_atom", [_]), _, _) := "Symbol"
-  pub def infer_ic(CCall("__prim_char_to_string", [_]), _, _) := "String"
-  pub def infer_ic(CCall("__prim_str_concat_all", _), _, _) := "String"
-  pub def infer_ic(CCall(f, args), env, ic) := call_ty(f, args, env, ic)
-  pub def infer_ic(CIf(_, t, e), env, ic) := branch_join([BP(t, infer_ic(t, env, ic)), BP(e, infer_ic(e, env, ic))])
-  pub def infer_ic(CBlock(stmts), env, ic) := infer_block(stmts, env, ic)
-  pub def infer_ic(CCase(scrut, arms), env, ic) := branch_join(arm_pairs(arms, infer_ic(scrut, env, ic), env, ic))
-  pub def infer_ic(CList(elems, tail), env, ic) := list_ty(join_all(infer_all(elems, env, ic)), list_elem(infer_tail(tail, env, ic)))
-  pub def infer_ic(CLambda(params, body), env, ic) := build_fn(param_types(params), infer_ic(body, extend_lenv(params, env), ic))
-  pub def infer_ic(CAtom(_), _, _) := "Symbol"
-  pub def infer_ic(CTuple(_), _, _) := "unknown"
-
-  # a bare identifier: its env type if bound, else a nullary constructor's sum type
-  # (`ic.ctors`), else `unknown` (Rian.Check's `Map.get(env,x) || ctor_type(ic,x)`).
-  def id_ty(x String, env Dict(String, String), ic Dict(Symbol, Dict(String, String))) String
-  def id_ty(x, env, ic)
-    if Prim.map_has(env, x) do
-      Prim.map_get(env, x)
-    else
-      ctor_type(ic, x)
-    end
-  end
-
-  # a call's result: a function-typed env var yields its return type; else an applied
-  # constructor's sum type (`ic.ctors`); else a non-generic named function's return
-  # (`ic.funs`); else `unknown`.
-  # precedence mirrors Rian.Check.infer(ECall): a function-typed env var yields its
-  # return; else an applied constructor's sum type (`ic.ctors`); else `called_ret_with`
-  # — a generic function's INSTANTIATED return (`ic.fsigs`) or a non-generic one's
-  # declared return (`ic.funs`); else `unknown`.
-  def call_ty(f String, args Vec(Core), env Dict(String, String), ic Dict(Symbol, Dict(String, String))) String
-  def call_ty(f, args, env, ic)
-    if Prim.map_has(env, f) do
-      call_ret(Prim.map_get(env, f))
-    else
-      case ctor_type(ic, f) do
-        "unknown" -> called_ret_with(f, args, env, ic)
-        ty -> ty
-      end
-    end
-  end
-
-  # `ic.ctors[name]` (a nullary or applied constructor's sum type), else `unknown`.
-  def ctor_type(ic Dict(Symbol, Dict(String, String)), name String) String := ic_lookup(ic, :ctors, name)
-
-  # a generic function (`ic.fsigs[f]` with type variables) instantiates its return
-  # from the call's argument types (ADR-0042); otherwise fall back to the non-generic
-  # `ic.funs` return. Mirrors Rian.Check.called_ret_with.
-  def called_ret_with(f String, args Vec(Core), env Dict(String, String), ic Dict(Symbol, Dict(String, String))) String
-  def called_ret_with(f, args, env, ic)
-    case fsig_lookup(ic, f) do
-      FsSome(FSig(_, _, [])) -> called_ret(ic, f)
-      FsSome(FSig(params, ret, tvars)) -> instantiate_ret(FSig(params, ret, tvars), infer_all(args, env, ic))
-      FsNone -> called_ret(ic, f)
-    end
-  end
-
-  # a non-generic named function's declared return type (`ic.funs[f]`); a return that
-  # is *itself* a type variable (or mentions one) is `unknown` — only `fsigs` can pin
-  # a generic return (Rian.Check.called_ret).
-  def called_ret(ic Dict(Symbol, Dict(String, String)), f String) String
-  def called_ret(ic, f)
-    ret := ic_lookup(ic, :funs, f)
-    if ret == "unknown" do
-      "unknown"
-    else
-      if has_tvar(ret) do "unknown" else ret end
-    end
-  end
-
-  # ── generic-return instantiation (port of Rian.Check.instantiate_ret) ──────
-  # `ic.fsigs[f]` is "params|ret|tvars" (params/tvars comma-joined) — the port's
-  # string encoding of `%{params, ret, tvars}`. Decode it, or FsNone when absent.
-  def fsig_lookup(ic Dict(Symbol, Dict(String, String)), f String) FsOpt
-  def fsig_lookup(ic, f)
-    raw := ic_lookup(ic, :fsigs, f)
-    if raw == "unknown" do
-      FsNone
-    else
-      FsSome(decode_fsig(raw))
-    end
-  end
-
-  def decode_fsig(raw String) FSig := mk_fsig(split_pipe(raw))
-
-  def mk_fsig(Vec(String)) FSig
-  def mk_fsig([params_str, ret, tvars_str]) := FSig(split_comma(params_str), ret, split_comma(tvars_str))
-  def mk_fsig(_) := FSig([], "unknown", [])
-
-  # unify each (declared-param-type, inferred-arg-type) to bind tvars, then substitute
-  # them in `ret`. A `ret` tvar the args can't pin -> the whole call is `unknown`
-  # (sound); a tvar absent from `ret` need not be pinned (`length(xs Vec(T)) Int53`).
-  def instantiate_ret(FSig, Vec(String)) String
-  def instantiate_ret(FSig(params, ret, tvars), arg_types)
-    binds := bind_all(params, arg_types, tvars, [])
-    if all_bound(filter_contained(tvars, ret), binds) do
-      subst_all(binds, ret)
-    else
-      "unknown"
-    end
-  end
-
-  def bind_all(Vec(String), Vec(String), Vec(String), Vec(Bind)) Vec(Bind)
-  def bind_all([], _, _, acc) := acc
-  def bind_all(_, [], _, acc) := acc
-  def bind_all([p | ps], [a | as], tvars, acc) := bind_all(ps, as, tvars, bind_tvar(p, a, tvars, acc))
-
-  # bind a bare tvar param to its arg type (first binding wins); recurse through a
-  # `Vec(T)`/`Vec(X)` structural match; an `unknown` arg or concrete param is inert.
-  def bind_tvar(p String, a String, tvars Vec(String), acc Vec(Bind)) Vec(Bind)
-  def bind_tvar(p, a, tvars, acc)
-    if a == "unknown" do
-      acc
-    else
-      if member_str(p, tvars) do
-        if has_bind(acc, p) do acc else [Bnd(p, a) | acc] end
-      else
-        if both_vec(p, a) do
-          bind_tvar(inner(p), inner(a), tvars, acc)
-        else
-          acc
-        end
-      end
-    end
-  end

-  def both_vec(p String, a String) Bool := starts_vec(Prim.str_chars(p)) and starts_vec(Prim.str_chars(a))
-
-  # does the codepoint list begin with "Vec(" (86,101,99,40)?
-  def starts_vec(Vec(Int53)) Bool
-  def starts_vec([86, 101, 99, 40 | _]) := true
-  def starts_vec(_) := false

-  def inner(s String) String := Prim.str_from_chars(drop_last(drop_n(4, Prim.str_chars(s))))

-  def drop_n(Int53, Vec(Int53)) Vec(Int53)
-  def drop_n(0, cs) := cs
-  def drop_n(_, []) := []
-  def drop_n(n, [_ | cs]) := drop_n(n - 1, cs)

-  def drop_last(Vec(Int53)) Vec(Int53)
-  def drop_last([]) := []

-  # the `tvars` that actually appear (as whole tokens) in `ret` need binding.
-  def filter_contained(Vec(String), String) Vec(String)
-  def filter_contained([], _) := []
-  def filter_contained([tv | rest], ret)
-    if word_contains(tv, ret) do

-  def all_bound([], _) := true

-  # substitute every binding's tvar (as a whole token) in `ret`.

-  def subst_all([], ret) := ret
-  def subst_all([Bnd(tv, ty) | rest], ret) := subst_all(rest, word_replace(tv, ty, ret))

-  def member_str(String, Vec(String)) Bool
-  def member_str(_, []) := false
-  def member_str(x, [y | rest]) := if x == y do true else member_str(x, rest) end

-  def has_bind(Vec(Bind), String) Bool
-  def has_bind([], _) := false
-  def has_bind([Bnd(p, _) | rest], x) := if p == x do true else has_bind(rest, x) end

-  # ── word-token utilities (word boundary == identifier-run boundary) ────────
-  # tokenize a type string into maximal word-runs ([A-Za-z0-9_]) and single
-  # non-word chars (kept verbatim), so substitution/containment is per-token.
-  def word_contains(tv String, ret String) Bool := member_str(tv, toks(Prim.str_chars(ret)))
-  def word_replace(tv String, repl String, ret String) String := concat_strs(map_replace(tv, repl, toks(Prim.str_chars(ret))))
-  def has_tvar(ret String) Bool := any_tvar_tok(toks(Prim.str_chars(ret)))

-  # ── error set #1: numeric mix (ADR-0035) — the first SELF-CHECKING gate ──────────
-  # The inference above never rejects; it infers `unknown` and moves on. This is the
-  # first port of a Rian.Check ERROR SET — the boundary check that turns the compiler
-  # from self-COMPILING into (partially) self-CHECKING. `Rian.Check.check_numeric_mix`:
-  # a `+`/`-`/`*` whose two operands are concretely a different numeric KIND (one
-  # int/uint, the other float) is REJECTED — a value never silently becomes a float.
-  # `num_mix` walks one clause body's Core and returns true iff such a mix exists.
-  # CONSERVATIVE: an operand inferred `unknown` (or non-numeric) never triggers — only a
-  # PROVABLE int↔float mix. The env is FIXED across the walk (no case-narrow / block-bind
-  # / lambda-extend as we descend), mirroring the reference's `scan_num_mix`.

-  # The THIRD build-loop gate (after exhaustiveness + capability) — the one that turns

-  # a float. Scoped to `d_func` (the inline `def f(p T) R := body` form); separate-clause

-  # ── driver Core → checker.rian Core projection (for `Checker.num_mix`) ──────────
-  # The driver's Core has 18 constructors and shapes (CIf over Blocks, Arm with a guard,
-  # CDot/CRemote/CStruct/CMap, …) that checker.rian's leaner Core lacks. `num_mix` only
-  # needs to (a) FIND `+`/`-`/`*` nodes and (b) infer their DIRECT operand types — so the
-  # mix-bearing nodes (CBin/CUnary, the leaves, real `__prim_*` CCalls) are preserved with
-  # checker's shape, while every structural node is collapsed to a `CCall("__x",
-  # children)` that `num_mix` still walks. The collapse uses only the driver's OWN Core
-  # constructors (whose runtime tags coincide with checker's for the preserved nodes), so
-  # the result types as `Core` AND never invents a CBin — it can therefore never cause a

-  # `unknown` under the collapse — the gate is merely more conservative there, never wrong.

-# `float → string` prim to format them like `Float.to_string` (so `/` float-division

-# `comptime(...)` call in place (its inner expression still folded). The corpus uses

-# wild/var/lit/char/atom/tuple/ctor/list/as/pin/struct/map. The Lower-internal
-# resolved nodes (`variant_lit`/`struct_lit`/`const_ref`) and the decl-resolved
-# `str_interp` / Rust-baked `rpat` are not surface, so they are out of scope.

-# renders the reference `Rian.Core` struct to the same string and diffs.

-# ===========================================================================
-# SELF-HOSTING — a Rian DECLARATION front-end, written in Rian (Stage 2)
-# ===========================================================================
-# Parses the declaration forms a program is made of into a `Decl` representation
-# that, projected to `Rian.IR` (the test), matches what `Rian.Decl.parse` builds
-# and is compiled + RUN by the real backend (`Rian.Beam.compile_ir/2`) — the
-# Stage-2 thesis (ADR-0063): a Rian front-end producing IR the existing backend
-# consumes, with no Elixir parse in the loop.
-#
-# Forms covered:
-#   type Name := V1 | V2(T, …)                         sum declarations
-#   struct Name(field Type, …)                         product (record) types
-#   mod Name do … end                                  module nesting (incl. `pub def`)
-#   def name(p [cap] Type, …) Ret [forall T, U: Bound] := expr   single typed clause
-#   def name(pat, …) [when g] := expr                  pattern clause (multi-clause)
-#   generics: `Ret forall T` / `Ret forall T, U: Eq + Ord` binders (ADR-0042),
-#             carried as `tvars`/`bounds` on the function head
-#   patterns: _ · var · Int literal · String/Char literal · Ctor(pat, …)
-#             · cons/list [] / [h | t] (nested)
-#   capabilities: val / iso / ref / tag (default val); parametric types `Vec(T)`
-#   exprs: binops (precedence climbing) · prefix - / not · calls · `.field` access
-#          · String/Char literals · labeled construction `Name(f: v)`
-#          · list construction `[x | acc]` · map literal `%{k: v, …}` (kept as a
-#            `MapE` node of `Label` fields; lowered to a Core map when emitting)
-#          · `if COND do THEN else ELSE end` (single-expr branches; ADR-0063)
-#          · `case SCRUT do PAT [when G] -> BODY … end` (single-expr arms; ADR-0063)
-#          · `with C <- E [, …] do BODY [else ARMS] end` — kept as a `With` node
-#            (preserving intent); the desugar to nested `case` is done when LOWERING
-#            the AST to Core, not here (ADR-0039)
-#
-# Out of slice (the remaining long tail of Rian.Decl):
-# negative-literal patterns, `alias`/`const`/`protocol`/`impl`,
-# doc-comments, and multi-statement block (`do … end`) function bodies.

-mod Decl do
-  type Tok :=
-      TNum(String) | TStr(String) | TIStr(Vec(IPart)) | TChar(Int53) | TId(String) | TKw(String) | TOp(String)
-    | TAnnot(String) | TLP | TRP | TLBracket | TRBracket | TLBrace | TRBrace | TMapOpen | TComma | TNL

-  # mirrors the lexer's interpolated-string token: literal segments + token-carrying holes.
-  type IPart := ILit(String) | IHole(Vec(Tok))
-
-  # expression AST — Num/Id/Bin/Unary/Call lower to Rian.Pratt's surface tuples;
-  # list construction is nil/cons (NilE / ConsE), flattened to `{:list_lit, …}` by
-  # the projection (the cons `{:tail, …}` tag would otherwise collide with patterns).
-  type Expr :=
-      Num(String) | Str(String) | Char(Int53) | Id(String) | Atom(String) | Bin(String, Expr, Expr)
-    | Unary(String, Expr) | Call(Expr, Vec(Expr))
-    | Dot(Expr, String) | Label(String, Expr)
-    | If(Expr, Expr, Expr)
-    | Case(Expr, Vec(CaseArm))
-    | With(Vec(WithClause), Expr, Vec(CaseArm))
-    | BlockE(Vec(Stmt))
-    | Tuple(Vec(Expr))
-    | MapE(Vec(Expr))
-    | Lam(Vec(String), Expr)
-    | Interp(Vec(ISeg))
-    | NilE | ConsE(Expr, Expr) | EErr
-
-  # an interpolation segment: a literal chunk or a hole expression to stringify.
-  type ISeg := SLit(String) | SHole(Expr)
-
-  # a multi-statement block body (`def f() T <nl> b := e <nl> e <nl> end`): a
-  # sequence of `name := expr` binds (SBind), `name Ty := expr` typed binds
-  # (STypedBind, ADR-0034 — the annotation enables the binding type gate), and bare
-  # expressions (SExpr) ending in a value. The projection (decl_fixpoint) lowers
-  # `BlockE` to Rian.Pratt's `{:block, [{:bind, n, e} | {:typed_bind, n, t, e} |
-  # {:expr, e}, …]}` (what `Pratt.parse_body` builds).
-  type Stmt := SBind(String, Expr) | STypedBind(String, String, Expr) | SExpr(Expr)
-
-  # clause PATTERNS — Wild/Var/Lit/Ctor lower straight to Rian.Decl's tuples
-  # (:wild / {:var,n} / {:lit,k} / {:ctor,c,ps}); list patterns are nil/cons
-  # (NilP / ConsP), flattened to `{:list, elems, :close | {:tail,p}}` by the test.
-  # StrP/CharP are literal patterns: a string pattern projects to `{:lit, s}` (like
-  # an int `Lit`), a char pattern to `{:char_lit, cp}`.
-  type Pat :=
-      Wild | Var(String) | Lit(Int53) | StrP(String) | CharP(Int53) | AtomP(String) | Ctor(String, Vec(Pat))
-    | TupleP(Vec(Pat))
-    | StructP(String, Vec(FldP))
-    | NilP | ConsP(Pat, Pat)
-
-  # a struct pattern field `field: pat` (symmetric with labeled construction).
-  type FldP := FP(String, Pat)
-
-  # a `case` arm — `pat [when guard] -> body`. Projects to Rian.Pratt's
-  # `{pat, guard | nil, body}` (CArm → nil guard; CArmG → the guard expr).
-  type CaseArm := CArm(Pat, Expr) | CArmG(Pat, Expr, Expr)
-
-  # a `with` clause — `PAT <- EXPR`. A `with` carries an ordered list of these,
-  # a body, and `else` arms (case-style). The desugar to nested `case` is a
-  # lowering concern (ADR-0039), so the AST keeps the clauses intact.
-  type WithClause := WC(Pat, Expr)
-
-  type Variant := V(String, Vec(String))
-  type Param := Par(String, String, String)
-  type PType := PT(String, Vec(Tok))
-  # a `forall` binder (ADR-0042): the tvar name + its protocol bounds (empty list
-  # when unconstrained). `forall T: Eq + Ord` -> TV("T", ["Eq", "Ord"]).
-  type TVar := TV(String, Vec(String))
-  # `pub?` (a Bool) is carried on the function head (DFunc/DSig) so `pub def`
-  # inside a `mod` projects to `Func.pub? = true` (exported on the BEAM); the
-  # `Vec(TVar)` carries the `forall` generics (empty when none).
-  type Decl :=
-      DType(String, Vec(Variant))
-    | DStruct(String, Vec(Param))
-    | DFunc(Bool, String, Vec(Param), String, Vec(TVar), Expr)
-    | DSig(Bool, String, Vec(Param), String, Vec(TVar))
-    | DClause(String, Vec(Pat), Expr)
-    | DClauseG(String, Vec(Pat), Expr, Expr)

-    | DUse(String)
-    | DConst(String, String, String)
-    | DRange(String, String, Int53, Int53)
-    | DOpaque(String, String)
-    | DProtocol(String, Vec(PMethod))
-    | DImpl(String, String, Vec(IMethod))
-    | DErr

-  # a protocol method signature: name + detokenized parameter string + return type

-  type PMethod := PM(String, String, String)
-
-  # an impl method clause: name + detokenized parameter string + detokenized body

-  type IMethod := IM(String, String, String, String)

-  # a generated `protocol`/`impl` def (the desugar output of `Rian.Protocol.expand`):

-  type PrnRes := PRN(Vec(Expr), Vec(Tok))
-  type Args := AP(Vec(Expr), Vec(Tok))
-  type DeclRes := DR(Decl, Vec(Tok))

-  type OneVar := OneV(Variant, Vec(Tok))

-  type ParamRes := PR(Param, Vec(Tok))
-  type Paren := Paren(Vec(Tok), Vec(Tok))

-# ===========================================================================
-# SELF-HOSTING SPIKE — the exhaustiveness gate (FULL), written in Rian
-# ===========================================================================
-# Goal (ADR-0063 §2; the gate that has most earned its keep): the complete
-# Maranget usefulness check `U(P, q)` — the Rian-written counterpart of
-# `Rian.Exhaustiveness.useful?/3`, fixpoint-locked against it in
-# `test/rian/exhaust_fixpoint_test.exs` over the full algorithm: single- and
-# multi-column matrices, constructors with arguments (specialised by arity),
-# wildcards, and signature completeness over finite vs infinite types.
-#
-# Patterns are `PWild | PCtor(name, args)` — lists (`nil`/`cons`), tuples, and
-# nullary sums are all just constructors, so this one representation covers them.
-# The typing environment (ctor→arity, ctor→type, type→signature) is passed as
-# structured data and searched linearly, so the port is FFI-free.
-#
-# Exhaustiveness is then `not useful(env, rows, [PWild, ...])` (the standard
-# Maranget reduction); the fixpoint test diffs `useful` directly against the
-# reference. The witness/counterexample pass (algorithm I) is the `:partial` tail.
-# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-
-mod Exhaust do
-  # A pattern: a wildcard, or a constructor applied to sub-patterns.
-  type Pat := PWild | PCtor(String, Vec(Pat))
-
-  # The result of the signature check: the head ctors cover the whole (finite)
-  # type, or they do not (incl. infinite/unregistered types).
-  type Sig := Complete(Vec(String)) | Incomplete
-
-  # The typing environment, searched linearly (FFI-free):
-  #   cdefs : each constructor's arity and owning type
-  #   tdefs : each finite type's full constructor set (absence => infinite)
-  struct CDef(name String, ar Int53, ty String)
-  struct TDef(ty String, ctors Vec(String))
-  struct Env(cdefs Vec(CDef), tdefs Vec(TDef))
-
-  # ── list / lookup helpers ──────────────────────────────────────────────
-  def append(Vec(Pat), Vec(Pat)) Vec(Pat)
-  def append([], ys) := ys
-  def append([x | xs], ys) := [x | append(xs, ys)]
-
-  def dup_wild(n Int53) Vec(Pat)
-  def dup_wild(0) := []
-  def dup_wild(n) := [PWild | dup_wild(n - 1)]
-
-  def member_str(Vec(String), String) Bool
-  def member_str([], _) := false
-  def member_str([x | xs], s)
-    if x == s do
-      true
-    else
-      member_str(xs, s)
-    end
-  end
-
-  def subset(Vec(String), Vec(String)) Bool
-  def subset([], _) := true
-  def subset([a | rest], present)
-    if member_str(present, a) do
-      subset(rest, present)
-    else
-      false
-    end
-  end
-
-  # CDef/TDef are structs (tagged maps) — read their fields, don't destructure.
-  def arity_of(Vec(CDef), String) Int53
-  def arity_of([], _) := 0
-  def arity_of([cd | rest], name)
-    if cd.name == name do
-      cd.ar
-    else
-      arity_of(rest, name)
-    end
-  end
-
-  def type_of(Vec(CDef), String) String
-  def type_of([], _) := ""
-  def type_of([cd | rest], name)
-    if cd.name == name do
-      cd.ty
-    else
-      type_of(rest, name)
-    end
-  end
-
-  def type_all(Vec(TDef), String) Vec(String)
-  def type_all([], _) := []
-  def type_all([td | rest], ty)
-    if td.ty == ty do
-      td.ctors
-    else
-      type_all(rest, ty)
-    end
-  end
-
-  # ── matrix operations ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
-  # Head constructor names present in the matrix (duplicates are harmless — only
-  # membership is used downstream).
-  def head_ctors(Vec(Vec(Pat))) Vec(String)
-  def head_ctors([]) := []
-  def head_ctors([row | rest]) := head_of(row, head_ctors(rest))
-
-  def head_of(Vec(Pat), Vec(String)) Vec(String)
-  def head_of([PCtor(c, _) | _], acc) := [c | acc]
-  def head_of([PWild | _], acc) := acc
-  def head_of([], acc) := acc
-
-  # Specialise by constructor `c`: keep rows that can match `c`, expanding args.
-  def specialize(Vec(Vec(Pat)), String, Env) Vec(Vec(Pat))
-  def specialize([], _, _) := []
-  def specialize([row | rest], c, env) := append_rows(spec_row(row, c, env), specialize(rest, c, env))
-
-  def spec_row(Vec(Pat), String, Env) Vec(Vec(Pat))
-  def spec_row([PCtor(d, args) | rest], c, env)
-    if d == c do
-      [append(args, rest)]
-    else
-      []
-    end
-  end
-  def spec_row([PWild | rest], c, env) := [append(dup_wild(arity_of(env.cdefs, c)), rest)]
-  def spec_row([], _, _) := []
-
-  # Default matrix: rows with a wildcard head, head column dropped.
-  def default_mat(Vec(Vec(Pat))) Vec(Vec(Pat))
-  def default_mat([]) := []
-  def default_mat([row | rest]) := append_rows(def_row(row), default_mat(rest))
-
-  def def_row(Vec(Pat)) Vec(Vec(Pat))
-  def def_row([PCtor(_, _) | _]) := []
-  def def_row([PWild | rest]) := [rest]
-  def def_row([]) := []
-
-  # append on matrices (Vec(Vec(Pat))).
-  def append_rows(Vec(Vec(Pat)), Vec(Vec(Pat))) Vec(Vec(Pat))
-  def append_rows([], ys) := ys
-  def append_rows([x | xs], ys) := [x | append_rows(xs, ys)]
-
-  # ── signature completeness ─────────────────────────────────────────────
-  def signature(env Env, present Vec(String)) Sig
-    case present do
-      [] -> Incomplete
-      [c | _] -> sig_check(env, c, present)
-    end
-  end
-
-  def sig_check(env Env, c String, present Vec(String)) Sig
-    sig_of(type_all(env.tdefs, type_of(env.cdefs, c)), present)
-  end
-
-  # an empty signature means infinite/unregistered -> Incomplete; otherwise
-  # complete iff the whole signature is present.
-  def sig_of(Vec(String), Vec(String)) Sig
-  def sig_of([], _) := Incomplete
-  def sig_of([a | more], present) := pick(subset([a | more], present), [a | more])
-
-  def pick(ok Bool, all Vec(String)) Sig
-    if ok do
-      Complete(all)
-    else
-      Incomplete
-    end
-  end
-
-  def is_empty(Vec(Vec(Pat))) Bool
-  def is_empty([]) := true
-  def is_empty([_ | _]) := false
-
-  # ── usefulness U(P, q) ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
-  pub def useful(Env, Vec(Vec(Pat)), Vec(Pat)) Bool
-  pub def useful(_, rows, []) := is_empty(rows)
-  pub def useful(env, rows, [PCtor(c, args) | qrest]) :=
-    useful(env, specialize(rows, c, env), append(args, qrest))
-  pub def useful(env, rows, [PWild | qrest])
-    case signature(env, head_ctors(rows)) do
-      Complete(ctors) -> any_useful(env, ctors, rows, qrest)
-      Incomplete -> useful(env, default_mat(rows), qrest)
-    end
-  end
-
-  # Is the wildcard query useful through ANY constructor of a complete signature?
-  def any_useful(Env, Vec(String), Vec(Vec(Pat)), Vec(Pat)) Bool
-  def any_useful(_, [], _, _) := false
-  def any_useful(env, [c | rest], rows, qrest)
-    if useful(env, specialize(rows, c, env), append(dup_wild(arity_of(env.cdefs, c)), qrest)) do
-      true
-    else
-      any_useful(env, rest, rows, qrest)
-    end
-  end
-end

-# ===========================================================================
-# SELF-HOSTING SLICE — the formatter's pretty-printing ENGINE, written in Rian
-# ===========================================================================
-# A Rian port of `Rian.Format.Doc` (the Wadler/Lindig strict pretty-printer that
-# drives line wrapping; ADR-0045). The Doc algebra + the linear worklist renderer
-# are pure recursion over lists/strings/ints — squarely in the self-hostable
-# subset — so they are the cleanest first slice of the formatter to bring into
-# Rian. Fixpoint-locked against `Rian.Format.Doc.render/2` in
-# `test/rian/format_doc_fixpoint_test.exs`: both engines build the same Doc from a
-# shared recipe (via these `pub` constructors) and must render byte-identical
-# output over a corpus.
-#
-# NOT yet ported (the remaining tail, BEAM-only by design): the trivia lexer, the
-# bracket CST, and the line/indent + chain-wrap lowering — they lean on the host
-# lexer and richer collections. See ADR-0045 / SELFHOST.md.
-# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-
-mod RianFormatDoc do
-  # render mode: a group is laid out flat (one line) or broken (with newlines)
-  type Mode := MFlat | MBreak
-
-  # the document algebra (mirrors Rian.Format.Doc):
-  #   DLine(s) is a break that becomes `s` when flat (" " = line, "" = softline);
-  #   DGroup(must_break, d) caches break-propagation; DIfBreak(b, f) picks by mode.
-  type Doc :=
-      DEmpty
-    | DText(String)
-    | DConcat(Vec(Doc))
-    | DNest(Int53, Doc)
-    | DLine(String)
-    | DHard
-    | DGroup(Bool, Doc)
-    | DSuffix(Doc)
-    | DIfBreak(Doc, Doc)
-
-  # a worklist entry: indentation, mode, document
-  type Item := It(Int53, Mode, Doc)
-
-  # ── public constructors (both engines build from the same recipe) ─────────
-  pub def dempty() Doc := DEmpty
-  pub def dtext(s String) Doc := DText(s)
-  pub def dconcat(ds Vec(Doc)) Doc := DConcat(ds)
-  pub def dnest(n Int53, d Doc) Doc := DNest(n, d)
-  pub def dline() Doc := DLine(" ")
-  pub def dsoft() Doc := DLine("")
-  pub def dhard() Doc := DHard
-  pub def dsuffix(d Doc) Doc := DSuffix(d)
-  pub def dif_break(b Doc, f Doc) Doc := DIfBreak(b, f)
-
-  # group: caches whether it must break (contains a hard break, propagated up)
-  pub def dgroup(d Doc) Doc := DGroup(has_hard(d), d)
-  pub def dgroup_forced(d Doc) Doc := DGroup(true, d)
-
-  # ── break propagation (Prettier's propagateBreaks) ────────────────────────
-  def has_hard(Doc) Bool
-  def has_hard(DEmpty) := false
-  def has_hard(DText(_)) := false
-  def has_hard(DLine(_)) := false

-# ===========================================================================
-# SELF-HOSTING — string-interpolation desugar (`${expr}`), written in Rian
-# ===========================================================================
-# Goal (ADR-0069 / ADR-0063 #2): the Rian-written counterpart of the DESUGAR in
-# `Rian.Interp.resolve` — rewrite a `${…}`-interpolated string into a plain
-# `<>`/stringify chain, choosing each hole's stringify path by the hole's STATIC
-# type. Fixpoint-locked against `Rian.Interp.resolve` in
-# `test/rian/interp_fixpoint_test.exs`.
-#
-# Factoring (honest scope): `Rian.Interp.resolve` couples two jobs — (1) INFER each
-# hole's type (`Check.infer`) and (2) DESUGAR by that type. Inference is a SEPARATE
-# pass already self-hosted in `compiler/checker.rian` (infer_ic). This port owns the
-# Interp-SPECIFIC half — the stringify-by-type + single-shot concat — taking each
-# hole's already-inferred type as input. The fixpoint test feeds it the very types
-# `Check.infer` produces, so the desugar is locked exactly against the oracle.
-#
-# Tails (vs the oracle): the `Show.float` auto-injection side-effect (Process flag),
-# `Float32`/no-Show RAISES (the port emits a marker call), and nested interpolation
-# inside a hole (the oracle resolves it first) — none exercised by the corpus.
-# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-
-mod Interp do
-  # ── surface expression AST (mirrors Rian.Pratt tuples / core.rian's Surface) ──
-  # holes carry an arbitrary Surface expression; the desugar treats it opaquely.
-  type Surface := SNum(String)
-                | SStr(String)
-                | SChar(Int53)
-                | SId(String)
-                | SAtom(String)
-                | SUnary(String, Surface)
-                | SBin(String, Surface, Surface)
-                | SCall(Surface, Vec(Surface))
-                | SLabel(String, Surface)
-                | SDot(Surface, String)
-                | SIf(Surface, Surface, Surface)
-                | STuple(Vec(Surface))
-                | SList(Vec(Surface), STail)
-                | SMap(Vec(SPair))
-                | SBlock(Vec(SStmt))
-                | SCase(Surface, Vec(SArm))
-                | SLambda(Vec(SParam), Surface)
-                | SCapArg(Int53)
-                | SCapture(Surface)
-                | SCaptureNamed(Surface, Int53)
-                | SWith(Vec(SClause), Surface, Vec(SArm))
-
-  type STail := TClose | TTail(Surface)
-  type SPair := SP(String, Surface)
-  type SStmt := SBind(String, Surface) | STypedBind(String, String, Surface) | SExpr(Surface)
-  type SGuard := GNone | GSome(Surface)
-  type SArm := SArm(SPat, SGuard, Surface)
-  type SClause := SClause(SPat, Surface)
-  type SParamTy := PtNone | PtSome(String)
-  type SParam := SParam(String, SParamTy)
-
-  type SPat := PWild
-             | PVar(String)
-             | PLitInt(Int53)
-             | PLitStr(String)
-             | PPChar(Int53)
-             | PPAtom(String)
-             | PPTuple(Vec(SPat))
-             | PCtor(String, Vec(SPat))
-             | PPList(Vec(SPat), PTail)
-             | PPStruct(String, Vec(PPair))
-             | PPMap(Vec(PPair))
-
-  type PTail := PtlClose | PtlTail(SPat)
-  type PPair := PPr(String, SPat)
-
-  # an interpolation part: a literal segment, or a hole carrying its expression.
-  type IPart := ILit(String) | IHole(Surface)
-
-  # ── the desugar ──
-  # `types` are the holes' inferred types in part order (the checker's output, fed in);
-  # `show` is the set of type names with an `impl Show for T`.
-  pub def desugar(parts Vec(IPart), types Vec(String), show Vec(String)) Surface
-  pub def desugar(parts, types, show) := concat_chain(drop_empty(resolve_parts(parts, types, show)))
-
-  def resolve_parts(Vec(IPart), Vec(String), Vec(String)) Vec(Surface)
-  def resolve_parts([], _, _) := []
-  def resolve_parts([ILit(s) | rest], types, show) := [SStr(s) | resolve_parts(rest, types, show)]
-  def resolve_parts([IHole(e) | rest], [t | ts], show) := [stringify(e, t, show) | resolve_parts(rest, ts, show)]
-  def resolve_parts([IHole(e) | rest], [], show) := [stringify(e, "unknown", show) | resolve_parts(rest, [], show)]
-
-  # stringify a hole by its static type (Rian.Interp.stringify).
-  def stringify(e Surface, ty String, show Vec(String)) Surface
-  def stringify(e, "String", _) := e
-  def stringify(e, "Bool", _) := SIf(e, SBlock([SExpr(SStr("true"))]), SBlock([SExpr(SStr("false"))]))
-  def stringify(e, "Char", _) := SCall(SId("__prim_char_to_string"), [e])
-  def stringify(e, "Float64", _) := SCall(SDot(SId("Show"), "float"), [e])
-  def stringify(e, ty, show)
-    if int_type(ty) do
-      SCall(SId("__prim_int_to_string"), [e])
-    else
-      if member_str(ty, show) do
-        SCall(SId("show"), [e])
-      else
-        # Float32 / no-Show / unknown: the oracle RAISES — the port emits a marker
-        # call (a documented tail; the corpus uses only stringifiable types).
-        SCall(SId("__interp_no_show"), [e])
-      end
-    end
-  end
-
-  # join the stringified parts: drop empty-string literals, then 0 -> "", 1 -> itself,
-  # ≥2 -> a single-shot `__prim_str_concat_all` (Rian.Interp.concat_chain).
-  def concat_chain(Vec(Surface)) Surface
-  def concat_chain([]) := SStr("")
-  def concat_chain([only]) := only
-  def concat_chain([x | rest]) := SCall(SId("__prim_str_concat_all"), [x | rest])
-
-  def drop_empty(Vec(Surface)) Vec(Surface)
-  def drop_empty([]) := []
-  def drop_empty([SStr("") | rest]) := drop_empty(rest)
-  def drop_empty([x | rest]) := [x | drop_empty(rest)]
-
-  def member_str(String, Vec(String)) Bool
-  def member_str(_, []) := false
-  def member_str(x, [y | rest]) := if x == y do true else member_str(x, rest) end
-
-  # `^U?Int\d*$` — an optional `U`, then `Int`, then zero or more digits.
-  def int_type(t String) Bool := after_u(Prim.str_chars(t))
-
-  def after_u(Vec(Int53)) Bool
-  def after_u([85 | rest]) := int_word(rest)
-  def after_u(cs) := int_word(cs)
-
-  def int_word(Vec(Int53)) Bool
-  def int_word([73, 110, 116 | rest]) := all_digits(rest)
-  def int_word(_) := false
-
-  def all_digits(Vec(Int53)) Bool
-  def all_digits([]) := true
-  def all_digits([c | rest]) := if c >= 48 and c <= 57 do all_digits(rest) else false end
-end

-# ===========================================================================
-# SELF-HOSTING — `Prim.*` -> `__prim_*` normalization, written in Rian
-# ===========================================================================
-# Goal (ADR-0047 §2, the reserved `Prim` intrinsic namespace): the Rian-written
-# counterpart of `Rian.Prim.normalize` — rewrite every surface `Prim.<name>(args)`
-# call into the canonical intrinsic `__prim_<name>(args)`, recursing through the
-# whole expression tree. Fixpoint-locked against `Rian.Prim.normalize` in
-# `test/rian/prim_fixpoint_test.exs`.
-#
-# Operates on the same `Rian.Pratt` surface AST as `core.rian` (the type below
-# mirrors it). Patterns carry no `Prim.*` calls, so the walk passes them through
-# unchanged (it only recurses into expression positions).
-#
-# Difference from the oracle (documented tail): `Rian.Prim.normalize` RAISES on an
-# unknown `Prim.<name>` (reserved namespace). This port has no host raise, so it
-# leaves an unknown `Prim.x` in place (still normalizing its args) — conservative,
-# never a miscompile. The compiler's own sources only use valid prims.
-# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-
-mod PrimNorm do
-  # ── surface expression AST (mirrors Rian.Pratt tuples / core.rian's Surface) ──
-  type Surface := SNum(String)
-                | SStr(String)
-                | SChar(Int53)
-                | SId(String)
-                | SAtom(String)
-                | SUnary(String, Surface)
-                | SBin(String, Surface, Surface)
-                | SCall(Surface, Vec(Surface))
-                | SLabel(String, Surface)
-                | SDot(Surface, String)
-                | SIf(Surface, Surface, Surface)
-                | STuple(Vec(Surface))
-                | SList(Vec(Surface), STail)
-                | SMap(Vec(SPair))
-                | SBlock(Vec(SStmt))
-                | SCase(Surface, Vec(SArm))
-                | SLambda(Vec(SParam), Surface)
-                | SCapArg(Int53)
-                | SCapture(Surface)
-                | SCaptureNamed(Surface, Int53)
-                | SWith(Vec(SClause), Surface, Vec(SArm))
-
-  type STail := TClose | TTail(Surface)
-  type SPair := SP(String, Surface)
-  type SStmt := SBind(String, Surface) | STypedBind(String, String, Surface) | SExpr(Surface)
-  type SGuard := GNone | GSome(Surface)
-  type SArm := SArm(SPat, SGuard, Surface)
-  type SClause := SClause(SPat, Surface)
-  type SParamTy := PtNone | PtSome(String)
-  type SParam := SParam(String, SParamTy)
-
-  # patterns are carried verbatim (no `Prim.*` calls live in a pattern position).
-  type SPat := PWild
-             | PVar(String)
-             | PLitInt(Int53)
-             | PLitStr(String)
-             | PPChar(Int53)
-             | PPAtom(String)
-             | PPTuple(Vec(SPat))
-             | PCtor(String, Vec(SPat))
-             | PPList(Vec(SPat), PTail)
-             | PPStruct(String, Vec(PPair))
-             | PPMap(Vec(PPair))
-
-  type PTail := PtlClose | PtlTail(SPat)
-  type PPair := PPr(String, SPat)
-
-  # ── the normalization walk ──
-  # The `Prim.<name>(args)` rewrite clause MUST precede the general call clause.
-  pub def normalize(Surface) Surface
-  pub def normalize(SNum(t)) := SNum(t)
-  pub def normalize(SStr(s)) := SStr(s)
-  pub def normalize(SChar(c)) := SChar(c)
-  pub def normalize(SId(n)) := SId(n)
-  pub def normalize(SAtom(a)) := SAtom(a)
-  pub def normalize(SUnary(op, x)) := SUnary(op, normalize(x))
-  pub def normalize(SBin(op, l, r)) := SBin(op, normalize(l), normalize(r))

-  pub def normalize(SCall(f, args)) := SCall(normalize(f), normalize_list(args))
-  pub def normalize(SLabel(n, e)) := SLabel(n, normalize(e))
-  pub def normalize(SDot(h, n)) := SDot(normalize(h), n)
-  pub def normalize(SIf(c, t, e)) := SIf(normalize(c), normalize(t), normalize(e))

-  pub def normalize(SCapture(b)) := SCapture(normalize(b))

-  # is left in place (the oracle raises — a documented tail). Args normalize either way.

-  def norm_prim_call(name, args)
-    if prim_name(name) do
-      SCall(SId("__prim_" <> name), normalize_list(args))

-      SCall(SDot(SId("Prim"), name), normalize_list(args))

-  end

-  def normalize_list(Vec(Surface)) Vec(Surface)
-  def normalize_list([]) := []

-  def normalize_tail(STail) STail

-  def normalize_pairs(Vec(SPair)) Vec(SPair)

-
-  def normalize_stmts(Vec(SStmt)) Vec(SStmt)
-  def normalize_stmts([]) := []
-  def normalize_stmts([SBind(n, e) | rest]) := [SBind(n, normalize(e)) | normalize_stmts(rest)]
-  def normalize_stmts([STypedBind(n, t, e) | rest]) := [STypedBind(n, t, normalize(e)) | normalize_stmts(rest)]
-  def normalize_stmts([SExpr(e) | rest]) := [SExpr(normalize(e)) | normalize_stmts(rest)]
-
-  def normalize_arms(Vec(SArm)) Vec(SArm)
-  def normalize_arms([]) := []
-  def normalize_arms([SArm(p, g, b) | rest]) := [SArm(p, normalize_guard(g), normalize(b)) | normalize_arms(rest)]
-
-  def normalize_guard(SGuard) SGuard

-# Goal (ADR-0063 §2 backend rung; ADR-0049/0055/0061): emit a whole Rust module

-# emission, fixpoint-locked against it in `test/rian/rust_module_fixpoint_test.exs`.

-# sum types become `enum`s. The emitter is precedence-aware (the reference's
-# `emit/2 -> {string, prec}` + `p/3`). The stage consumes Core that is already
-# RESOLVED (variant construction -> `Enum::Ctor`, ctor patterns carry their enum)

-# parser/Core stage's job and capability lowering is the (self-hosted) capability
-# stage's. Structs (decl/construction/field access) and closed + cons lists are
-# now covered, as are generic `<T: Clone>` signatures + a bare-tvar return clone
-# (`-> T` clones the borrowed body) and list PATTERNS (`[h | t]` -> the slice
-# rest-pattern `[h, t @ ..]`) with the slice-element clone rebind (a used head
-# binder is `let h = h.clone();`-rebound to an owned value). The non-generic
-# call-site owned→borrow coercion is also in: an owned `vec![…]` argument passed to
-# a `&`-typed parameter is `&`-wrapped (`takes(&vec![1, 2])`, via `borrow_prog`). The

-# (`P(k: a, …)` -> `Pair::P { k: a.clone(), … }`). Parametric-enum monomorphization
-# (ADR-0061) is in: a parametric sum lowers to `enum Name<K: Clone, …>` (`generics`), and
-# every parametric type name in a signature is spliced to its instantiation at identifier
-# boundaries (`mono_ty`/`splice_one`, a char-scan port of `Rian.Lower.rustify_parametric`)

-  # assignable machinery already locked for the return-type set (error set #2).

-  # function a VALID return so `check_return` (which runs before `check_binds` in the

-  # PROTOCOL-BOUND violation (Rian.Check.check_bounds, ADR-0042 §2). At a call to a

-  # `bounds_bad/5` instantiates the callee's tvars from the argument types (`bind_all`,
-  # reused from generic-return inference) and returns `true` iff a bound `T: P`
-  # instantiates `T` to a CONCRETE type with no `impl P for that-type`.
-  #
-  # The port needs two tables the reference builds in `program_ic`: `fbounds` (a bounded
-  # function's tvars/param-types/bounds) and `impls` (protocol → implementing types). The
-  # test derives BOTH from the real `Check.program_ic`, projects them to the port's tuple
-  # shape, and feeds the caller's body Core to `bounds_bad`.
-  #
-  # LOCK: for each corpus program the port's `bounds_bad` over the caller's body must

-defmodule Rian.CheckerNumMixFixpointTest do
-  # async: false — loads compiler/checker.rian into the VM via :code.load_binary.
-  use ExUnit.Case, async: false

-  alias Rian.{Beam, Core, Check, Pratt}

-  # Self-hosting fixpoint (ADR-0063) for the type checker's FIRST ERROR SET — numeric
-  # mix (ADR-0035). `compiler/checker.rian`'s inference (`infer_ic`) never rejects; it
-  # infers `unknown` and moves on. `num_mix/3` is the first port of a Rian.Check
-  # BOUNDARY check — the thing that turns the self-built compiler from self-COMPILING
-  # into (partially) self-CHECKING: it returns `true` iff a clause body contains a
-  # `+`/`-`/`*` whose two operands are concretely a different numeric KIND (one
-  # int/uint, the other float) — a value never silently becomes a float.
-  #
-  # LOCK: for each corpus function, the port's `num_mix` (over the body's Core, the
-  # clause's param env, an empty `ic`) must AGREE with whether the REAL
-  # `Rian.Check.check/1` reports the numeric-mix error. The corpus uses param/literal
-  # operands only, so the empty `ic` is irrelevant (an `ic`-dependent operand — a call
-  # to a float-returning function — is the documented tail, where the port is merely
-  # MORE conservative, never wrong). The reference's inference is itself already
-  # equivalence-locked (checker_infer_fixpoint_test), so agreeing operand types compose
-  # into an agreeing mix decision.
-
-  setup_all do
-    {:ok, mod} = Beam.load(File.read!("compiler/checker.rian"), :rian_checker_nummix_fixpoint)
-    {:ok, mod: mod}
-  end
-
-  # {label, body expression, param env, the full function (for the reference)}.
-  # NEGATIVE = a provable int↔float mix → BOTH the port and Rian.Check must flag it.
-  @negative [
-    {"Int + float-lit", "a + 1.5", %{"a" => "Int64"}, "def f(a Int64) Float64 := a + 1.5"},
-    {"Int - float-lit", "a - 2.5", %{"a" => "Int64"}, "def f(a Int64) Float64 := a - 2.5"},
-    {"Int * Float param", "a * b", %{"a" => "Int64", "b" => "Float64"},
-     "def f(a Int64, b Float64) Float64 := a * b"},
-    {"float-lit + Int", "1 + x", %{"x" => "Float64"}, "def f(x Float64) Float64 := 1 + x"},
-    {"UInt * float-lit", "u * 2.0", %{"u" => "UInt32"}, "def f(u UInt32) Float64 := u * 2.0"},
-    {"Char + float-lit", "c + 1.5", %{"c" => "Char"}, "def f(c Char) Float64 := c + 1.5"},

-    # error to fire first) — isolating the gate while proving the walk recurses.
-    {"mix nested in comparison", "(a + 1.5) > a", %{"a" => "Int64"},

-  ]

-  # POSITIVE = NO provable mix → BOTH must pass. Covers same-kind arithmetic, non-arith
-  # operators, conservative `unknown` operands, and the div/rem exclusion.

-    {"Int + Int", "a + b", %{"a" => "Int64", "b" => "Int64"},
-     "def f(a Int64, b Int64) Int64 := a + b"},
-    {"Float - Float", "a - b", %{"a" => "Float64", "b" => "Float64"},

-    {"untyped operands (unknown)", "a + b", %{}, "def f(a, b) Int64 := a + b"},
-    {"bare var, no arith", "a", %{"a" => "Int64"}, "def f(a Int64) Int64 := a"},

-  defp inj(%Core.ENum{text: t}), do: {:c_num, t}
-  defp inj(%Core.EStr{value: v}), do: {:c_str, v}
-  defp inj(%Core.EChar{value: c}), do: {:c_char, c}
-  defp inj(%Core.EId{name: n}), do: {:c_id, n}
-  defp inj(%Core.EUnary{op: op, arg: a}), do: {:c_unary, op, inj(a)}
-  defp inj(%Core.EBin{op: op, left: l, right: r}), do: {:c_bin, op, inj(l), inj(r)}
-  defp inj(%Core.ECall{fun: %Core.EId{name: f}, args: as}), do: {:c_call, f, Enum.map(as, &inj/1)}
-  defp inj(%Core.EIf{cond: c, then: t, else: e}), do: {:c_if, inj(c), inj(t), inj(e)}
-  defp inj(%Core.EBlock{stmts: stmts}), do: {:c_block, Enum.map(stmts, &inj_stmt/1)}
-  defp inj(%Core.ECase{scrut: s, arms: arms}), do: {:c_case, inj(s), Enum.map(arms, &inj_arm/1)}

-  end

-  describe "num_mix agrees with Rian.Check.check_numeric_mix (the lock)" do
-    test "every NEGATIVE case is flagged by BOTH the port and the reference", %{mod: mod} do
-      for {label, body, env, src} <- @negative do
-        assert ref_mix(src), "reference did not flag the mix in #{label}: #{inspect(src)}"
-
-        assert port_mix(mod, body, env),

-
-    test "every POSITIVE case is passed by BOTH the port and the reference", %{mod: mod} do

-      end
-    end
-
-    test "port and reference agree on every corpus entry (the equivalence lock)", %{mod: mod} do
-      for {label, body, env, src} <- @negative ++ @positive do
-        assert port_mix(mod, body, env) == ref_mix(src),
-               "num_mix DIVERGED from Rian.Check on #{label}: #{inspect(src)}"
-      end
-    end
-  end
-end

-  # STEP 3 (verification bridge) — the driver's surface→Core lowering is
-  # equivalence-locked to `Rian.Core` via the verified `selfhost_core` oracle.
-  #
-  # The composition driver (compose_real_sum.rian) lowers selfhost_decl's
-  # surface to `selfhost_beam`'s Core with its own `lower_surface`/`lower_pat` — the

-  # locked only BEHAVIORALLY (the build runs identically to Rian.Beam). This bridge
-  # locks it STRUCTURALLY: for the same source, the driver's Core, rendered to the
-  # canonical s-expression, equals what `Rian.Core.from_expr` produces AND what the
-  # `selfhost_core` port emits (itself locked to `Rian.Core` in core_fixpoint_test).

-  # body (`BlockE`) projects each statement onto Rian.Pratt's `{:bind,…}`/`{:expr,…}`,
-  # matching what `Pratt.parse_body` builds from Rian.Decl's `;`-joined body string.
-  defp to_body({:block_e, stmts}), do: {:block, Enum.map(stmts, &stmt/1)}
-  defp to_body(body), do: {:block, [{:expr, ce(body)}]}

-  defp stmt({:s_bind, n, e}), do: {:bind, n, ce(e)}
-  defp stmt({:s_expr, e}), do: {:expr, ce(e)}

-  # convert the front-end's nil/cons list PATTERNS to Rian.Decl's `{:list, …}` shape
-  # (var/lit/ctor/wild lower directly); flatten the cons chain.
-  defp cp({:ctor, c, args}), do: {:ctor, c, Enum.map(args, &cp/1)}
-  defp cp({:str_p, s}), do: {:lit, s}
-  defp cp({:char_p, code}), do: {:char_lit, code}
-  defp cp({:atom_p, n}), do: {:atom, n}
-  defp cp({:tuple_p, ps}), do: {:tuple, Enum.map(ps, &cp/1)}
-  defp cp(:nil_p), do: {:list, [], :close}
-
-  defp cp({:cons_p, _, _} = c) do
-    {elems, tail} = flat_p(c)
-    {:list, Enum.map(elems, &cp/1), tail}
-  end
-
-  defp cp(leaf), do: leaf
-
-  defp flat_p(:nil_p), do: {[], :close}
-  defp flat_p({:cons_p, h, :nil_p}), do: {[h], :close}
-
-  defp flat_p({:cons_p, h, {:cons_p, _, _} = t}) do
-    {es, tl} = flat_p(t)
-    {[h | es], tl}
-  end
-
-  defp flat_p({:cons_p, h, t}), do: {[h], {:tail, cp(t)}}

-  # convert the front-end's nil/cons list EXPRESSIONS to `{:list_lit, …}` (recurse
-  # into bin/unary/call); num/id lower directly.
-  defp ce(:nil_e), do: {:list_lit, [], nil}
-
-  defp ce({:cons_e, _, _} = c) do
-    {elems, tail} = flat_e(c)
-    {:list_lit, Enum.map(elems, &ce/1), tail}
-  end
